newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore, Hungary to sign investment and tax deal.
newsitem.headline: Singapore, Hungary to sign investment and tax deal.

text.p: Singapore and Hungary said on Wednesday they would sign agreements to guarantee investments and avoid double taxation during a visit by the Hungararian prime minister.
Prime Minister Gyula Horn arrives in Singapore on Wednesday for a three-day visit to boost trade and investment. It is the the first visit to Singapore by a Hungarian prime minister.
A Singapore-Hungary business forum will be held on Thursday where several commercial agreements will be signed between companies of both countries, a Hungarian embassy official said.
A Singapore government statement said the two countries would also sign an agreement to avoid double taxation.
Horn will be accompanied by Minister for Finance Peter Medgyessy, Minister for Trade and Tourism Szabolcs Fazakas, and Minister without Portfolio (Privatisation) Judit Csiha.

Bilateral trade between Singapore and Hungary in 1996 rose about 50 percent against the previous year to Singapore $125 million (US$87 million). Singapore exported S$88 million worth in goods to Hungary and Hungary exported S$37 million in return.
Singapore investments in Hungary's medical, real estate and manufacturing industries have so far amounted to about S$42 million, the embassy official told Reuters. ($1 =S$1.44)
